points.description: States that non-conventional machining requires high-skill (skilled/trained) labour.
points.partial_credit: Vague mention, e.g. 'needs skilled operators' without clear link to labour/skill level, gets half.

points.description: States that it is inefficient because of a low metal removal rate (MRR), i.e. slow material removal.
points.partial_credit: Says 'inefficient' or 'slow' without naming low metal removal rate gets half.

points.description: States that it is generally an expensive (high cost) process.
points.partial_credit: Vague cost wording, e.g. 'costly equipment' only, gets half.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for naming all three drawbacks: high-skill labour, low metal removal rate, and high cost; any one correct drawback from these earns its share, and clear synonyms are accepted. Round the total to the nearest half mark, so two correct drawbacks give about 1 to 1.5 and one gives about 0.5 to 1. Give no marks for unrelated drawbacks, such as 'cannot cut hard materials' or 'causes tool wear'.
